```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# Every number of the expected-numbers section is read from the committed data
# files of the case, so that the guide and the pages cannot drift apart; readr
# rather than datawizard::data_read(), which reads empty cells as "" rather than NA.
fmt <- \(x, d = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d) |> sub(pattern = "^-", replacement = "−")

curve <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/spec_curve.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
analysts <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/analysts5.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
marks <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/reference_marks.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
deviations <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/menu_deviations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
outcomes <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_outcomes.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
power <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_power.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ri <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_ri.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
n_emails <- nrow(readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/housing_audit.csv", show_col_types = FALSE))

ref <- datawizard::data_filter(curve, is_reference)
ref_all <- datawizard::data_match(curve, tibble::tibble(comparison = "white", population = "all",
                                                        uncoded = "drop", model = "lpm", adjust = "none"))
an <- \(id, col) analysts[[col]][analysts$id == id]
mark <- \(id) marks$b_pp[marks$id == id]
shift <- \(axis, option, col = "shift_mean") deviations[[col]][deviations$axis == axis & deviations$option == option]
pw <- \(design, gap) power$power[startsWith(power$design, design) & power$gap_pp == gap]
reply_gap <- datawizard::data_filter(outcomes, outcome == "reply" & contrast == "hispanic")
# The SCORE replication on the scale of the course (display_replication.csv)
replication <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_replication.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
rep_val <- \(population_code, authorities_code, col) {
  replication[[col]][replication$population == population_code &
                       replication$authorities == authorities_code]
}
sgn <- \(x, d = 1) paste0(if (round(x, d) >= 0) "+" else "", fmt(x, d))

# The Task 3 test of 8PTRZ: Hispanic against all other names among the coded replies
coded <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/audit_original.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_filter(!is.na(ProperName)) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(hispanic_name = grepl("^Hispanic", TreatmentGroup))
tab_8ptrz <- stats::xtabs(~ hispanic_name + ProperName, data = coded)  # r-style: keep – the table that chisq.test() takes
chi_yates <- unname(stats::chisq.test(tab_8ptrz)$statistic)
chi_plain <- unname(stats::chisq.test(tab_8ptrz, correct = FALSE)$statistic)

# The Task 3 test of 25N5D: Hispanic against white names among the delivered
# emails, a missing reply counted as no greeting, with and without the
# continuity correction that prop.test() applies by default
counts_25n5d <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/audit_original.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_filter(!is.na(Response_Dichotomous) & !grepl("^black", TreatmentGroup)) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(hispanic_name = grepl("^Hispanic", TreatmentGroup),
                          greeted = Response_Dichotomous == 1 & ProperName %in% 1) |>
  datawizard::data_summary(greetings = sum(greeted), emails = n(), by = "hispanic_name")
prop_yates <- unname(stats::prop.test(counts_25n5d$greetings, counts_25n5d$emails)$statistic)
prop_plain <- unname(stats::prop.test(counts_25n5d$greetings, counts_25n5d$emails, correct = FALSE)$statistic)

# Placement as try_spec() prints it: the specifications further below zero,
# with the tolerance of the helpers, so that the logit twin of the reference
# specification ties with it
placement_ref <- sum(curve$b_pp < ref$b_pp - 1e-9)
other_max <- deviations |>
  datawizard::data_filter(axis != "population") |>
  datawizard::data_summary(m = max(shift_max)) |>
  datawizard::data_extract("m")
```

::: {.callout-note}
**This document is for the facilitator.** It is rendered with the site but left out of the navbar, so nothing on the site links to it. It holds the run sheets of the formats of the housing-audit case – the short session (deck `slides/housing-short.qmd`), the one-day workshop (deck `slides/housing-one-day.qmd`) and the Extended course, whose second day is the workshop – with the checks before a delivery, the expected numbers and the fallbacks. The participant pages under `tracks/` give the instructions for each part and its total length, and the timings of each step are kept here: the run sheets below for the parts of each format, [the preparation table](#preparation) for the pages "Before the session" and "Before the day", and [the self-study route](#run-self-study) for the stages of the self-study track.
:::

---

## The formats {#formats}

| Format | Track | Taught in | What it leaves out |
|---|---|---|---|
| Short session, two halves | `housing-short` | the browser lab only | installation, the class chart, Task 5 |
| One-day workshop, four parts | `housing-one-day` | the browser lab, the workspace as an option | nothing of the five tasks |
| Extended course, three days | `housing-extended` | the workspace, with the browser lab on day 2 | nothing; day 2 is the workshop |
| Self-study, five stages | `self-study` | the workspace | the class, but not the class chart |

In every format the participant chooses which of the five reanalyses to reproduce in Task 3. Only the workshop, on its own or as the second day of the Extended course, sends results to the class chart. The segments that differ by format read the `deck:` map in the YAML of each deck through Quarto conditional content (`when-meta="deck.short"` and the like), so a change of wording for one format is made in the segment, inside the span or the div that carries that condition.

---

## The delivery lifecycle {#delivery-lifecycle}

Between deliveries the opening page advertises no delivery. Scheduling one takes three steps, and resetting after one takes two.

**Scheduling.**

- [ ] Fill the `delivery:` block in `_variables.yml` (date, venue, event, mode, registration URL), set `track:` to one of the track slugs of the table above, and set `active: 'true'`. Render the opening page (`quarto render index.qmd`), and it shows a "Next delivery" callout with a link to the track. Set `active: 'false'` again afterwards.
- [ ] Decide on recording. If you record, record the talk only, announce it at the start of each recorded stretch, and pause it for the hands-on tasks. Nothing in the day depends on the recording either way.
- [ ] Decide which way the day leans. The deck of the workshop keeps one optional run on the `d` key, `methods`: the six-slide methods tutorial after the menu and the two slides of multiverse background after Task 4, of which the multiverse background is also the one optional run of the short session. To make the run part of the main flow, list it under `core-runs:` in the YAML of the deck and render it again; a run that is not listed stays optional and can still be switched on live.

**Resetting, before the next delivery of the workshop.**

- [ ] Export the responses Sheet (File → Download → CSV) and keep it as a dated snapshot, for example `cases/housing/data/class_results_2026-11-06.csv`.
- [ ] Clear the data rows of the Sheet, so that the chart opens almost empty for the next class. Do not touch the Form, the Worker or the field schema; only the rows change from one class to the next.

---

## Before the day

### The preparation of participants {#preparation}

The page "Before the session", "Before the day" or "Before the course" of each format lists these steps. The pages give no times, so if the joining instructions need them, put them there.

| Step | Short session | One-day workshop | Extended course |
|---|---|---|---|
| The case study | required | required | required |
| The browser lab, opened once, with the setup cell of Task 1 run | required | required | – |
| R, an IDE and the workspace, until `R/check_setup.R` prints OK | – | required | required |
| Getting started with R (`tools/r.qmd` on the AR4DS site) | – | required | required |
| The modules on the IDE, on Quarto and on Git and GitHub (AR4DS site) | – | recommended | the reading of days 1 and 3 |
| The exercise overview | – | recommended | – |

### The week before

- [ ] **The browser lab.** Every format is taught mainly in the browser lab, so check it on the published site in a real browser: the engine loads, the setup cell of Task 1 runs, and the cells of each of the five analysts of Task 3 print the right value (the expected numbers are at the end of this guide).
- [ ] **The workspace.** The workspace is the repository `CodeMoreh/replication-lab-housing`, whose zip is linked from the setup page of the AR4DS site, the cheatsheet and the slide on the browser lab and the workspace in Part 1. Download the zip once from its public address and confirm that it unzips into `replication-lab-housing-main`, and that a change made on the site since the last delivery has reached the workspace where it should. The short session does not need it.
- [ ] **The class-results Form**, for the workshop only. Out of the box, the housing helpers submit to the results Form that every case shares, the one set up for the EU-frames case, and the housing chart reads the same Sheet through the same Worker, keeping only the rows whose label carries the word `housing` after the tag. That works as it stands. Clear the Sheet of the rows of earlier deliveries before the day (the data rows below the header of the tab "Form Responses 1"; the Form keeps working), because the EU-frames chart reads every row and would draw housing rows as unclassed diamonds. The alternative, which keeps the two classes apart for good, is a Form of its own, about twenty minutes once, following [`facilitator/live-results-setup.md`](https://github.com/CodeMoreh/ar4ds-eu/blob/main/facilitator/live-results-setup.md) in the repository of the EU-frames site.
- [ ] **Joining instructions.** Send the address of the track page, the case study as the pre-reading, and the request to open the browser lab once on the machine that each participant will bring, with a laptop charger. For the workshop and the Extended course add the setup page, with the request to run `R/check_setup.R` until it prints OK, the module Getting started with R and the help page.
- [ ] **The tab switching.** Click once through the sequences that you run live: the deck and the browser lab in every format; the deck, the specification menu and the decision map, and the Multiverse page in the short session and the workshop.
- [ ] **The room.** Confirm the projector, the power sockets, the wifi for visitors (webR downloads its engine and packages on first load) and whether the room has Vevox or a similar response tool. The slides say "type in chat" for the held answers; in the room, decide in advance what "chat" means, as the cue sheet below sets out.

### The night before

- [ ] Render the pages that have changed, page by page (pCloud breaks a full render), and check that the opening page, the track pages, the case pages and the deck of the day are current; push if the site is published.
- [ ] **The browser lab, cold.** Open the live page of the lab in a private window on a connection like that of the venue, time the load of the R engine, and run the setup cell and the cells of one analyst of Task 3.
- [ ] **The live-results loop**, for the workshop. Submit one test result from the browser lab (`try_spec()`, then `submit_exploration(nickname = "test-row")`), confirm that it reaches the Sheet, press *Run Code* on the class chart of the [Multiverse](../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd#class-results) page and find the test circle. Then delete the test row from the Sheet.
- [ ] **The workspace, as a participant meets it**, for the workshop and the Extended course. Download the zip afresh, unzip it, open the folder in your IDE, run `source("R/check_setup.R")` (every line OK, the last at −19.97 points) and render the report. For the Extended course, also commit once and render the report from a clean session.
- [ ] **The public record**, for the workshop. Confirm that the three addresses of the records slide load without an account: doi.org/10.7910/DVN/1HOVTU, osf.io/3a8bg and osf.io/2ug8x, and that the final report of the replication is findable from the last one, because it is the target of the three-minute search in Part 4. The de-identified data of the replication are in its sub-component osf.io/xseqg, for anyone who asks.
- [ ] **The fallback zip**, for the workshop and the Extended course. Put the workspace zip on a USB stick, for anyone whose download fails in the room.
- [ ] Prepare the catch-up card of the format (in its run sheet) as a ready-to-paste text, and charge everything.

### Opening the room

- [ ] Put the address of the course site, the browser lab and the cheatsheet on the screen or the whiteboard as people arrive, with the wifi details.
- [ ] Hand out the green and red sticky notes, or open the response tool, and say what each means: green, working; red, stuck.
- [ ] Keep the tabs of the day ready: the deck and the browser lab in every format, and in the short session and the workshop the [decision map](../cases/housing/map.qmd), the [specification menu](../cases/housing/menu.qmd) and the [Multiverse](../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd) page.
- [ ] If you record, announce it now and say what is and is not recorded.

## Deck controls {#deck-controls}

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| space, right arrow or clicker | next slide, always exactly one: the deck is linear, so that no clicker press can skip a part |
| **`d`** | switch between the **full** and the **lean** deck, live; in lean mode the optional slides are taken out of the deck and every key skips them |
| **`]`** and **`[`** | jump to the next or the previous part |
| **`g`** | jump bar: type a few letters of any slide title and press Enter |
| **`s`** | speaker view, with the notes, a timer and the next slide |
| **`f`**, **`esc`** | full screen, and the slide overview |

The readout at the top right names the part and the position, and its badge shows the state of the deck: green **full**, burgundy **optional** on a slide of an optional run, amber **lean** when the runs are off, with a burgundy dot where a run has been lifted out. Adding `?depth=0` to the address opens the deck lean. The first slide of each optional run carries a small grey link that jumps to where the main flow resumes.

## Run sheet – the short session {#run-short}

The short session runs on `slides/housing-short.qmd` as two halves of about seventy-five minutes with a break of fifteen, entirely in the browser lab. It has no Task 2 at the keyboard (the estimand statement is written as a held answer, and the graph is followed on the slides), sends nothing to the class chart and has no Task 5; `tracks/housing-short/after.qmd` points to them for afterwards. Its one optional run is the two slides of multiverse background.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Draft clock times for CM to adjust**, here for an afternoon slot from 14:00 GMT.
:::

| Segment | Elapsed | Example clock (GMT) |
|---|---|---|
| First half – The claim and its reproduction | 0:00–1:15 | 14:00–15:15 |
| Break | 1:15–1:30 | 15:15–15:30 |
| Second half – Exploration and replication | 1:30–2:45 | 15:30–16:45 |

### First half (75′)

| Rel. | Segment | What I do | What participants do | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00 | Welcome, what you do not need (3′) | The premise and the plan. "Open the browser lab now." | Open the lab in a tab. | Late arrivals: the address on the screen. |
| 0:03 | The matrix, SCORE in brief, Multi100 (12′) | The four cells; SCORE on one slide; what an analyst received, the two tasks, the common scale. | Listen. | – |
| 0:15 | Hands-on 1: the setup check (5′) | A quick confirmation in the lab. | Run the setup cell; 1,014 rows. | A lab that will not load: another browser, then the shared screen. |
| 0:20 | The paper and the five analysts (18′) | Define the original authors (OAs); the design, the email, what came back, the claim; the five analysts and their table. | Listen. | – |
| 0:38 | The estimand and the graph (12′) | The held estimand statement; the graph; the box around the reply; every delivered email. | Write the statement; send on "go". | Never compressed. |
| 0:50 | The instruction and analyst no. 6 (6′) | The Multi100 instruction, what it left open, the choice of analyst. | Choose an analyst. | Encourage a spread across the five, so that the held answer shows several matches rather than one. |
| 0:56 | Hands-on 3: the reproduction (14′) | Drive one analyst in the lab on the shared screen; circulate. Then the held answer: "type the analyst and the value, hold it, go". | Complete one cell; send on "go". | Wait for most of the class. |
| 1:10 | The continuity correction, reproducibility and choice (5′) | The defaults of `chisq.test()` and `prop.test()`, the base group of EWFMI; the class against the five analysts. | – | – |

### Second half (75′)

| Rel. | Segment | What I do | What participants do | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00 | The menu and the two models (14′) | The eleven decisions, the curve of 64, the ground rules; a difference in proportions; the linear probability model and the logit. | Choose a decision to vary. | – |
| 0:14 | Hands-on 4: Task 4 (20′) | "Try two or three, one decision at a time; read one refusal; rerun the one you would defend." | `try_spec()` two or three times; `my_experiments()`. | Say that nothing is submitted, so `submit_exploration()` is skipped. |
| 0:34 | Your own small multiverse and the curve (8′) | Name what Task 4 was; optionally the origins of the idea; the curve of the claim and the published results placed on it. | Watch. | – |
| 0:42 | The placement (5′) | The held placement: "rerun the one you would defend, read your placement, hold it, go". | Read and send. | A placement of 32 or more comes from counting every delivered email. |
| 0:47 | What moved the estimate (6′) | The shifts, and the denominator. | – | – |
| 0:53 | The SCORE replication (13′) | The design, the result, the two studies compared, power, the three Rs on this paper, robustness against replicability. | Listen; argue. | The robustness and replicability slide is the lesson of the session. |
| 1:06 | Close and feedback (7′) | Two points, the single path, what you take, the form; the class chart and Task 5 as work for afterwards. | Feedback. | End on time. |

### Cutting order and what is never cut {#cutting-short}

For a slot of two hours, cut in this order: the multiverse background; the SCORE slide of the first half at speed; the slide on the linear probability model and the logit, to one sentence; the placement; and the replication to three slides (the design, the result, and robustness against replicability). The reproduction and the exploration keep their full time.

**Never cut:** the five analysts and their table; the held estimand statement; the box around the reply; the reproduction and its held answer; one try of `try_spec()` that changes the emails counted; robustness against replicability.

## Run sheet – the one-day workshop {#run-one-day}

The day runs on `slides/housing-one-day.qmd`, mainly in the browser lab, with the workspace as an option. Part 1 sets out the claim and the credibility of social science, Part 2 the estimand and the causal graph, Part 3 the reproduction, and Part 4 the robustness exercise: the menu, the class chart with its two waves of submissions, the curve of the claim, the replication and the declared analysis.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Draft clock times for CM to adjust.** The default starts at 10:00 GMT and keeps breaks of thirty minutes, an hour and thirty minutes, so the day ends at 17:45. The parts are of unequal length: the reproduction is the shortest, and robustness the longest, because it holds the two tasks with submissions. The pages of the participants give no times, so the times of a delivery go in the joining instructions. Shorter breaks need the text of the break slides changed as well (`slides/_segments/shared/_break1.qmd`, `slides/_segments/housing/_lunch-reading.qmd`, `_break-afternoon.qmd`).
:::

| Segment | Elapsed | Clock (GMT) |
|---|---|---|
| Part 1 – The claim and credibility | 0:00–1:30 | 10:00–11:30 |
| Break | 1:30–2:00 | 11:30–12:00 |
| Part 2 – The estimand and the causal graph | 2:00–3:15 | 12:00–13:15 |
| Lunch | 3:15–4:15 | 13:15–14:15 |
| Part 3 – The reproduction | 4:15–5:25 | 14:15–15:25 |
| Break | 5:25–5:55 | 15:25–15:55 |
| Part 4 – Robustness | 5:55–7:45 | 15:55–17:45 |

**Two stretches of the deck are optional**, marked on screen and switched in one keystroke: the methods tutorial after the menu (six slides) and the multiverse background after Task 4 (two slides). The timings below assume that you walk about half of each.

### Part 1 – The claim and credibility (90′)

| Rel. | Segment | What I do | What participants do | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00 | Welcome, the two kinds of aim, what you do not need (6′) | The premise in two sentences: *Nature* asked three times whether social science holds up, I was inside one of the papers, and today you sit where I sat. Walk the aims slide. "Open the browser lab now." | Open the lab, or the workspace in their IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.). | Late arrivals: a nod and the address on the screen, never a restart. |
| 0:06 | Talk: what social science is for, and why it is called a crisis (10′) | Claims and checking; false positives and forking paths; the evidence from replications; incentives and questionable research practices, and why the problem is structural rather than fraud. | Listen. | – |
| 0:16 | Talk: the red-card study (4′) | The question, the design, and the twenty-nine estimates. | Watch. | The study returns in Part 2 as a single row, so tell it in full only here. |
| 0:20 | Talk: the vocabulary and open research (10′) | Replication crises; the data × analysis matrix; repeatability and credibility; the quick check, two slides, answered aloud; open-research practices. | Answer the quick check. | The matrix is the slide to copy down. If the segment runs long, the open-research table compresses to one sentence a row. |
| 0:30 | Talk: SCORE in brief (6′) | The programme and its three studies on one slide, and the finding that the three do not travel together. | Listen. | The first day of the Extended course takes SCORE in full. |
| 0:36 | Talk: Multi100 from the inside (8′) | What an analyst received, the two tasks, results on a common scale. | Listen. | The five analysts of the case come in Part 2. |
| 0:44 | Talk: the paper (16′) | Define the original authors (OAs) here. The question, the design, the email, what came back by name, four outcomes, the claim with its two ellipses. | Listen; ask. | The two ellipses decide the comparison group later, so read both aloud. |
| 1:00 | The browser lab and the workspace (5′) | The two places to work, with the same tasks and the same numbers; what the tools cannot do. | Check that the lab has loaded. | – |
| 1:05 | Task 1, the warm-up and the break (25′) | "Get to the point where a line of R runs and the data are in front of you; take the break for it if you need to." Circulate. Stay in the room through the break for red notes. | The setup cell of the lab and the warm-up on the three Rs, or `source("R/check_setup.R")`, every line OK, the last at −19.97 points. | Anyone whose workspace is still stuck at the end of the break moves to the browser lab, or to the zip on the USB stick. |

### Part 2 – The estimand and the causal graph (75′)

| Rel. | Segment | What I do | What participants do | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00 | Talk: the five analysts (8′) | The five placed by their gaps, then the table: five questions behind two verdicts. | Watch. | Never rush this pair: it sets up the rest of the day. |
| 0:08 | Talk: estimands (12′) | Two studies beside our five; four estimands in the red-card study; the spread with and without a fixed estimand; under-specified questions; the steps of Lundberg and colleagues. | Listen. | The figure with and without a fixed estimand is the point of the segment. |
| 0:20 | Talk: the causal-graph crash course (14′) | Confounder, mediator, collider; the stories behind one correlation; open and closed paths; total and direct effects; selection and feedback. | Listen. | If running long, selection and feedback drops to one sentence. |
| 0:34 | Talk: the claim (14′) | The estimand statement and the first held answer: "write your statement, hold it, go"; read three or four aloud. Then the graph, the box around the reply, and every delivered email. | Write the statement; send on "go". | The held answer is never compressed. A split between the replies and every delivered email is the same split as among the five analysts; say so. |
| 0:48 | Hands-on 2: Task 2 (27′) | Counting the emails, the estimand statement written out, then the graph cells of the lab or `R/dag_starter.R`: the arrow from the name to the greeting, the adjustment sets, the paths with `Z = "reply"`. | Count, write, finish the graph, two sentences. | At 1:05, if the class is behind, switch to demonstration: run it on the shared screen, and they finish over lunch. |
| 1:15 | Lunch | Post the return time. | Lunch. | A hard stop. |

### Part 3 – The reproduction (70′)

| Rel. | Segment | What I do | What participants do | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00 | Re-entry and the instruction (10′) | A visual sweep; the catch-up card on screen. The Task 2 instruction of Multi100 word for word, what it left open, and analyst no. 6 with the choice of analyst. | Rejoin; choose an analyst. | Do not wait past 0:05. Encourage a spread across the five. |
| 0:10 | Hands-on 3: Task 3, the reproduction (20′) | Drive one analyst in the lab on the shared screen beside them; circulate. Then the second held answer: "type the analyst and the value, hold it, go". | Complete one cell; send on "go". | The matching values, analyst by analyst, are the point of the beat, so wait until most of the class has one. A failing machine goes to the browser lab. |
| 0:30 | Defaults, reproducibility and choice (8′) | Why every value matches its record to the third decimal (the defaults of `chisq.test()` and `prop.test()`, the base group of EWFMI), and why five analysts writing their own code did not agree. | Listen. | Leave the question of the choices open for the menu of Part 4. |
| 0:38 | What a reproduction needs (10′) | The data under a licence, the code, the defaults, someone who tries; the published model and the blinded thirds of the public file. | Listen; ask. | The point is that open data can still stop short of the published number, by design. |
| 0:48 | Hands-on 3b: a second reproduction (17′) | "Choose a second analyst who differs from your first in one decision." | Reproduce a second analyst; compare the gaps. | If the class is slow, demonstrate UYV3F beside 25N5D on the shared screen. |
| 1:05 | Discussion (5′) | "Which of your two answers the claim as SCORE selected it?" | Answer. | The answer leads into the menu after the break. |
| 1:10 | Break | Leave the browser lab open. | Break. | – |

**The catch-up card**, for the re-entry to Part 3:

> Just back? You have missed nothing that you cannot recover: (1) if Task 2 is unfinished, keep the estimand statement that you wrote in chat and run the graph cells as they stand; (2) Task 3 is the reproduction – run the cell that reads the file, choose one analyst, work through the cells of that analyst, and compare your value with the table above the cells; (3) if you finish, reproduce a second analyst. Put up a red note and I will come to you.

### Part 4 – Robustness (110′)

| Rel. | Segment | What I do | What participants do | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00 | The menu (12′) | The eleven decisions in three groups, the five that vary on the curve, the curve of 64, the ground rules. | Start choosing which decision interests them. | Present the options off the curve as decisions to think through, each answering another question or this one less well; the decision map gives the reason for each. |
| 0:12 | The methods (8′, part optional) | A difference in proportions; the linear probability model and the logit. Optional: odds ratios, standard errors, four tests, the randomisation test, covariates, subgroups. | Listen; ask. | The compressible segment: if Part 3 overran, take time from here, not from Task 4. |
| 0:20 | Hands-on 4: Task 4, exploring the menu (20′) | "Try several, read what each does, then submit the one you would defend." Suggest `try_spec(model = "three_group")` so that people read a refusal. Keep the Multiverse page on screen and press *Run Code* as the open circles land. | `try_spec()` three or four times; `my_experiments()`; `submit_exploration()`. | Everyone submits a mark, because the next segments read them. Say twice that this is exploration and that Task 5 is the preregistered analysis. |
| 0:40 | Your own small multiverse and the curve (6′) | Name what Task 4 was; optionally the origins and the garden of forking paths; then the curve of the claim and the published results placed on it. | Watch. | – |
| 0:46 | The class multiverse and the placement (9′) | Refresh the class chart; the question bank (below). Then the third held answer: "rerun your submitted specification, read your placement, hold it, go". | Find their mark; read and send their placement. | Participants without a submission use the reference specification, whose placement is `r placement_ref`. |
| 0:55 | What moved the estimate (5′) | The shifts by option, then the curve coloured by the emails counted. | Connect the step to their own choice. | – |
| 1:00 | The SCORE replication (12′) | The design, the result, the two studies compared, power, the three Rs on this paper, robustness against replicability. | Listen; argue. | The robustness and replicability slide is the lesson of the day; never compress it. |
| 1:12 | Critics and preregistration (7′) | The critics; one correct analysis and how to identify it; what preregistration settles; exploration against declaration. | Listen; ask. | If the clock is tight, the identification slide goes to one sentence. |
| 1:19 | Archiving and the public record (7′) | Archiving and registering; the Multi100 preregistration; the two templates; the records slide with the three-minute search of the replication report; the eight AsPredicted questions. | Search the report; read. | The target of the search: not significant "approximately 93 percent of the time". If time is short, show it on the shared screen. |
| 1:26 | Hands-on 5: preregistration, run and report (18′) | Called from the front: complete fields 1–5, copy the cell or render the report, then the fourth held answer, "declared". Count aloud. Move on at about 80% declared or at eight minutes. Then `run_spec()` and `report_result()`; press *Run Code* as the filled circles land. | Declare, run, submit. | Never cut the declaration. Re-declaring a specification already explored is allowed, and the block must say so. |
| 1:44 | Close and feedback (6′) | Two points from the literature; the single analytical path; what you take with you; the feedback form, with the chart on screen. | Feedback. | End on time. |

### Cutting order and what is never cut {#cutting-one-day}

When time runs short, cut from the optional runs before anything else, so that the time comes out of a tutorial before it comes out of a task.

- **Part 1** – at 0:20, cut the open-research table to one sentence a row. At 1:00, the slide on what the tools cannot do goes to one sentence.
- **Part 2** – at 0:20, drop selection and feedback to one sentence. At 1:05, Task 2 becomes a demonstration, finished over lunch.
- **Part 3** – at 0:48, the second reproduction becomes the work of the early finishers, and the discussion goes to one question.
- **Part 4** – at 0:12, the methods run stays off. At 0:20, Task 4 shortens to two calls of `try_spec()` and a submission, but everybody still submits. At 0:40, skip the multiverse background. At 1:19, show the three-minute search on the shared screen instead of setting it.

**Never cut:** the five analysts and their table; the held estimand statement; the box around the reply; the reproduction and its held answer; the Task 4 submission; robustness against replicability; the preregistration moment.

## Run sheet – the Extended course {#run-extended}

The Extended course is three days, with the one-day workshop as its second day (`tracks/housing-extended/`). The first day is the same for every case of AR4DS and is given from decks of the AR4DS site; the third day teaches the methods of this case and ends with the report of each participant. A two-day version drops the third day and leaves the methods to self-study.

::: {.callout-warning}
**In preparation.** The decks of the first and the third days are being written (November 2026). Until they exist, each session runs from the module named beside it, which is also its reading. The durations are drafts for CM to adjust.
:::

**Day 1 – Open research and the tools.**

| Session | Reading | Draft |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Credibility and the three Rs | the glossary of `resources.qmd` | 75′ |
| 2. SCORE and Multi100 | the pages on SCORE and Multi100 and on the Multi100 article, AR4DS site | 60′ |
| 3. Repositories and data sources | `companion/data-sources.qmd`, `companion/repositories.qmd` | 60′ |
| 4. R, taught live on the housing-audit data | `tools/r.qmd`, AR4DS site | 75′ |
| 5. Positron, in the workspace | `tools/ide.qmd`, AR4DS site | 45′ |
| 6. Quarto, on the report of the workspace | `tools/quarto.qmd`, AR4DS site | 60′ |

**Day 2 – The workshop**, run as in its own run sheet above. After the first day, Part 1 can take SCORE and Multi100 at speed and give the time to Task 1 and Task 2.

**Day 3 – The methods and your report.**

| Session | Reading | Draft |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Audit experiments | `companion/experiments.qmd` | 75′ |
| 2. Binary outcomes | `companion/binary-outcomes.qmd` | 60′ |
| 3. Bayesian estimation | `companion/bayesian.qmd` | 60′ |

In the session on the report, each participant opens the workspace, turns its folder into a repository with the completed preregistration block of Task 5 as the first commit, writes the report around the declared analysis, renders it from a clean session and commits each step. Publishing the rendered report is optional, at the end of the day.

## The self-study route {#run-self-study}

The self-study track runs without a facilitator, and each stage page gives the total of its stage and nothing finer, because the time that a stage takes depends on the reader. The stages use the deck of the one-day workshop.

---

## The held answers {#held-answers}

The class writes an answer, holds it and releases it together: the estimand statement (every format), the reproduced value of Task 3 (every format), the placement (the short session and the workshop) and "declared" before the preregistered run (the workshop only). Holding the answers keeps each one independent of the others, and releasing them together is what produces the matching values after the reproduction. The slides say "type in chat"; the cue sheet below says what that means in the room.

**The reproduction moment.** Each participant chooses one of the five analysts and runs the code of that analyst in Task 3, in the lab or in the workspace. When most of the class has a value: "Type the analyst and the value, hold it … go." Everyone who chose the same analyst should show the same value, and each value should match its record: $\chi^2$ = `r fmt(an("8PTRZ", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` for 8PTRZ, z = `r fmt(an("UYV3F", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` for UYV3F, z = `r fmt(an("EWFMI", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` for EWFMI and $\chi^2$ = `r fmt(an("25N5D", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` for 25N5D, with `r fmt(an("P9W8Y", "statistic_refit"), 3)` on 2 degrees of freedom for P9W8Y, which has nothing on record. A participant with `r fmt(chi_plain, 2)` for 8PTRZ or `r fmt(prop_plain, 2)` for 25N5D has passed `correct = FALSE`, which is the opening line of the next slide. A z of `r fmt(-an("EWFMI", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` for EWFMI means that the Hispanic names are not the base group. A participant with another number has usually kept a different set of rows; check the filter against the table above the cells.

## In person and online {#cue-sheet}

The materials are the same in both settings. What changes is how people answer, flag trouble and pair up.

| Beat | In person (Newcastle) | Online |
|---|---|---|
| Held answers | the response tool of the room if it has one; otherwise written on a card and held up on "go" | typed in chat, sent on "go" |
| Working or stuck | green and red sticky notes on the laptop lid | a green circle or "STUCK" in chat |
| Rescues | the facilitator circulates | the problem shown on the shared screen |
| The live chart (the workshop) | on the projector, and on the laptops | everyone opens the Multiverse page |
| Form links (the workshop) | on the screen | pasted in chat |
| Breaks | the countdown slide and the time aloud | the countdown slide and "back at :xx" in chat |

## Fallbacks {#fallbacks}

Each row names the first move, not the only one, and every ladder ends at a point from which the session can carry on.

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| **The browser lab stalls** | The ladder of the [cheatsheet](../cases/housing/cheatsheet.qmd): a hard reload and the cells above run again, then a second browser, then the shared screen. In the workshop the last rung is the by-hand lookup, in which the facilitator reads the five choices off `spec_curve.csv` and submits the row through the Form, so that everyone still gets a mark. |
| **An installation fails on the day** | The browser lab holds the whole exercise and gives the same numbers; the participant carries on there, and the workspace survives for later. |
| **The workspace download fails in the room** | The zip on the USB stick. |
| **The wifi fails** | The workspace runs offline once its packages are installed, so the tasks continue for anyone who has it; the others follow the shared screen. In the workshop, collect the printed results (the tag, the label, `b`, `se`, `t`, `df`, `n`, `r`) and submit them through the Form when the network returns. The browser lab needs the network for its first load. |
| **The live chart fails** (the workshop: Form, Worker, CORS) | The chart falls back to the committed `cases/housing/data/class_results.csv`, which holds only its header. Pull the Sheet as CSV, put it in place of that file, render the Multiverse page locally and share the screen. The static curve and the reference marks at the top of the page are enough for the debrief. Submissions are safe in the Sheet whatever happens to the chart. |
| **The OSF is slow during the three-minute search** | Show the report of the replication on the shared screen; the beat still works. Nothing in the tasks depends on the OSF. |
| **A participant has lost their tag** (the workshop) | It is in `.class-tag` at the root of the workspace; in the lab, `report_result(nickname = "their-tag")` reuses it. |

## Expected numbers {#expected-numbers}

- **Task 1.** The setup cell of the lab: 1,014 rows and −19.97 percentage points. The last check of `R/check_setup.R`: the reference specification reproduces at `r fmt(ref$b_pp, 2)` percentage points.
- **Task 2.** `r format(n_emails, big.mark = ",")` emails, 23 bounced, 991 delivered, 563 replies, 5 without a greeting code, 558 coded. Greeted by name among the coded replies: white 61.1%, Black 56.1%, Hispanic 41.2%; Santiago lowest at 37.1%. The graph: with every delivered email counted, the adjustment set is empty, because the name was assigned at random; the paths with `Z = "reply"` report the paths through the official and through the community as open. Adding the community to `Z` closes the second, and nothing can close the first, because nobody observed the official.
- **Task 3**, on the public file `audit_original.csv`. 8PTRZ: $\chi^2$ = `r fmt(chi_yates, 3)` on `r an("8PTRZ", "n_recorded")` coded replies with the continuity correction, `r fmt(chi_plain, 3)` without it. UYV3F: z = `r fmt(an("UYV3F", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` on `r an("UYV3F", "n_recorded")` coded replies to Hispanic and white names. EWFMI: z = `r fmt(an("EWFMI", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` on `r an("EWFMI", "n_recorded")` coded replies, the row of the white names against the Hispanic base group. 25N5D: $\chi^2$ = `r fmt(prop_yates, 3)` on `r an("25N5D", "n_recorded")` delivered emails with the continuity correction of `prop.test()`, `r fmt(prop_plain, 3)` without it. P9W8Y: no recorded statistic; the likelihood-ratio test of the three groups gives $\chi^2$ = `r fmt(an("P9W8Y", "statistic_refit"), 3)` on 2 degrees of freedom for `r an("P9W8Y", "n_refit")` coded replies, the value in the text of the report of the analyst.
- **The reference specification** (white names, replies, uncoded dropped, linear model, no covariates): `r fmt(ref$b_pp, 2)` points (`r fmt(ref$rate_hisp)`% against `r fmt(ref$rate_comp)`%), t = `r fmt(ref$stat, 2)` on `r ref$df` df, n = `r ref$n`. Its twin on every delivered email: `r fmt(ref_all$b_pp, 2)` points (`r fmt(ref_all$rate_hisp)`% against `r fmt(ref_all$rate_comp)`%), n = `r ref_all$n`.
- **The curve.** `r nrow(curve)` specifications, all below zero and all significant at 5% under the test of the model, from `r fmt(min(curve$b_pp))` to `r fmt(max(curve$b_pp))` points; the largest p is `r fmt(max(curve$p), 4)`, and the largest randomisation p is `r fmt(max(curve$p_ri), 4)`. Counting every delivered email moves the estimate by `r fmt(shift("population", "all"), 2)` points on average (from `r fmt(shift("population", "all", "shift_min"), 2)` to `r fmt(shift("population", "all", "shift_max"), 2)`); every other decision by at most `r fmt(other_max, 2)`. No pair changes its sign or its significance.
- **Placement.** The reference specification is placed at `r placement_ref`: no specification of the curve lies further below zero, and the logit without covariates ties with it. A placement of 32 or more comes from counting every delivered email, because all 32 specifications that count the replies lie further below zero.
- **The reference marks.** OAs 2017 `r fmt(mark("OA"))` points (z = −3.73, N = 549); 8PTRZ `r fmt(mark("8PTRZ"))`; UYV3F `r fmt(mark("UYV3F"))`; EWFMI `r fmt(mark("EWFMI"))`; 25N5D `r fmt(mark("25N5D"))`; P9W8Y `r fmt(mark("P9W8Y"))`, placed by the course refit because Multi100 recorded no statistic for it. The published model refitted on the blinded thirds: `r fmt(mark("OA_blinded"))` points, not on the chart.
- **Replies.** The gap in any reply between Hispanic and white names is `r fmt(reply_gap$b_pp)` points, two-sided p = `r fmt(reply_gap$p, 2)`; the paper reports p = .11 with a one-tailed test.
- **Randomisation.** Reshuffling the names among the coded replies gives gaps between `r fmt(quantile(ri$b_pp, 0.025))` and `r fmt(quantile(ri$b_pp, 0.975))` points in 95% of `r format(nrow(ri), big.mark = ",")` reshuffles.
- **Power.** The original comparison, about 181 replies a group at a white share of 61%: `r fmt(pw("original", 20), 2)` for a gap of 20 points, `r fmt(pw("original", 13), 2)` for 13, `r fmt(pw("original", 10), 2)` for 10. The replication, 369 a group: `r fmt(pw("replication", 10), 2)` for 10 points.
- **The replication** (from its final report, osf.io/2ug8x): 3,050 authorities emailed, 1,811 replies; on the 1,243 replies of the authorities matched to census data, logit with the demographic covariates of the paper from the 2018 ACS (no Hard Email), b = 0.098 (SE 0.149), z = 0.66, p = 0.511 on a random draw of 738, and z = 0.44, p = 0.657 on all 1,243. The preregistered linear model was not significant "approximately 93 percent of the time". At most +2.45 points in favour of the Hispanic names. The plan was registered on 14 May 2020 (osf.io/v6wd8); the report lists the logit with covariates and the exclusion of the county authorities as deviations from it. The de-identified data are public at osf.io/xseqg (folder "Public Data": `Audit_Deidentified.dta`, the analysis do-file and a dictionary, licence unstated, so the course links to them and does not copy them). On the scale of the course (`cases/housing/data/display_replication.csv`), the gap is `r sgn(rep_val("replies", "all", "b_pp"))` points among all `r format(rep_val("replies", "all", "n"), big.mark = ",")` replies (`r fmt(rep_val("replies", "all", "rate_hisp"))`% against `r fmt(rep_val("replies", "all", "rate_comp"))`%), `r sgn(rep_val("replies", "sub-county", "b_pp"))` among the `r format(rep_val("replies", "sub-county", "n"), big.mark = ",")` replies of sub-county authorities, and `r sgn(rep_val("all", "all", "b_pp"))` points among all `r format(rep_val("all", "all", "n"), big.mark = ",")` emails in the de-identified file, none of them significant (smallest p = `r fmt(min(replication$p), 2)`). The logit with covariates in thirds on the 1,243 sub-county replies that carry every covariate (one of the 1,244 lacks the poverty third) gives b = 0.051, z = 0.45, column 4 of the report.
- **The five analysts.** Three concluded "evidence for the claim" in Task 1 of Multi100 (8PTRZ, UYV3F, EWFMI) and two "no evidence either way" (25N5D, apparently judging the claim by the twenty points of the abstract; P9W8Y, whose Task 1 model tested the female names only).

## Debrief questions {#debrief}

Choose by what the class shows, not by the order below. Questions 1 to 3 and 8 need the class chart of the workshop; the others work in every format.

1. **The step in the curve.** "Who counted every delivered email? What question does your estimate answer that the estimate of the paper does not, and which one is the claim?"
2. **The decision that did nothing.** "Who changed the model from the linear probability model to the logit and found that the estimate barely moved? Why does it barely move here, when the coefficients look so different?"
3. **Placement.** "Your placement puts you among 64 justifiable alternatives. What does an analyst at the end of the curve owe the reader that an analyst in the middle does not?"
4. **The two verdicts of no evidence.** "Two analysts ticked 'no evidence', although the work of each shows a significant gap. What were they judging the claim by?"
5. **The reproduction.** "Everyone who chose the same analyst got the same value. What would have had to be missing for that to fail: the data, the code, or a default?"
6. **Robustness against replication.** "Every specification on these data finds the gap; the replication did not. Which result should a housing authority act on, and what would you want to know first?"
7. **The names.** "Santiago and Gabriela against Joe Garcia and Michael Hernandez. What does a name manipulate besides ethnicity?"
8. **How preregistration felt.** "Did writing the block before running change how the result felt when it landed? Would you have chosen differently after the exploration?"

## After the session

- [ ] After the workshop, run the reset of the delivery lifecycle at the top of this guide: export the Sheet as a dated snapshot and clear its rows.
- [ ] Export the responses of the feedback form.
- [ ] Note for the next delivery: which segment ran longest; whether the estimand statement landed (could people write one, and did the held answers split on the emails counted); how the class spread across the five analysts in Task 3; in the workshop, how many declarations came before the proceed rule and whether every participant submitted a mark; which rungs of the fallback ladder were used; whether webR held on the venue wifi.
